stem: A trellised canopy has become even in height but interior access and airflow are now poor. Which decision best reflects canopy-management tradeoffs?
choices: Keep adding branches until most open canopy space is occupied because height uniformity is the primary goal of trellising and added coverage generally improves light capture.
Adjust branch placement or selectively remove obstructive growth to preserve access and airflow while maintaining useful canopy coverage.
Raise room humidity slightly because more humid air can reduce stress associated with dense interior foliage and restricted access during later canopy development.
Leave the canopy unchanged because once height is uniform, later density differences have limited effect on management quality if the upper surface remains evenly filled.
rationale: Canopy architecture is multi-objective: light distribution, access, airflow, and manageable density matter alongside height uniformity.
